issues.description: The symbol display_start is described and used as the base address of the frame buffer, but the solution's set_pixel uses [display_start] (the memory contents at that label) when computing the pixel address. This contradicts the intended use (an address/label value) and also differs from how display_start is used elsewhere in the solution (main uses mov esi, display_start to obtain the address). Using [display_start] yields the stored 32-bit value at that buffer start instead of the buffer's address and can produce an incorrect pointer calculation.
issues.suggestedFix: Treat display_start as an address, not as memory content. In set_pixel replace 'add eax, [display_start]' with 'add eax, display_start' (or load the base address into a register first, e.g. 'mov esi, display_start; add esi, eax; mov [esi], ecx'). Ensure the addressing is consistent with main's calculation (which uses mov esi, display_start).
